title: the DSG Deepearth areas 18-19
audit_comment: The DSG Deepearth areas 18-19 pin Area 18 (the Steam-Heated Caverns with their hot-stream chute, the six caves, the superheated north tunnel, the fire giant clan and the geysers) and Area 19 (the Chambers of Fire with their fissure eruptions, the mephits, fire bats and magmen, and the remote cavern of toil).
include_after: #include "rules/dsgarea8.h"  // R541: the DSG Deepearth areas 16-17 pins
audit_anchor: // ---- R227: the wis mental save wiring audit ----

DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 16-17, printed pp. 88-89 (pdf 89-90) -
Area 16 the Mid-Level Caverns (the 1,000-ft spiral stairway
with 10-ft width, 1-ft-deep stairs, 8-inch drops, hollow
10-ft shaft, no guardrail; the living caves; the drapery
central cave ringed by 12+ smaller caves; the steep west
descent - 20-ft-wide cavern, 1d6x10-ft cliffs, two 3-ft
pinches; the clear pools, largest 50 ft, commonly 20-30 ft
deep; wilderness status with pech/jermalaine/derro/drow
passing through; the monster caves - greater basilisk +
mimics central, bowlers, trappers, xorn, piercers, rock
reptiles, scum creepers, mud men in the flanks; fresh
water/stuffy air/fungi; the Area 14 copper-iron veins
streaking the draperies green/red; and the mud men's
enchanted stream - potion of healing from its niche, magic
lost to any container), and Area 17 the Lower Lake (the
12x13-mile cavern, 600 ft high, bottom 500 ft water; the
ceiling spout from the Upper Lake drain; the inaccessible
shoreline, tunnel mouth 50 ft above the surface; the
northern river 100 ft wide, 1d10+10 deep, ceiling 20-50
ft; the silt floor; six underwater caves 100+ ft down; the
aboleth-kuo-toa war; the kuo-toan southern domed city and
inter-lake path; ~300 aboleth in the northern floating city
with river-mouth guards; the fresh-water kraken - 40-ft
entrance tunnel, 50 mixed-race slaves with a truce,
tailing-stone pile; the >100,000-gp gold dust at 500 ft
under the spout; the drain plunge - 2d6 rounds submerged,
100-ft fall, 6d6 non-native halved on breath save, 3d6
native negated on save; the aboleth city - 1,000-ft mucous
disk, six slim towers, drain-holed wall, 20-30-ft lairs
with 1 entrance, ~100-ft clan halls/nurseries/prisons with
6 3-ft entrance holes, half water/half air with perch
ledges, slave races held apart, Three Clans halls, 40-ft
buoyancy disk). A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads
agree on every number (djvu ~lines 11260-11493, capture
idx 400-412; the capture '1dlO + 10' settled by the djvu
as 1d10 + 10). 60 inlines (44 consts + 16 bools), header
rules/dsgarea8.h, prefix dnaj, no table. DELIVERY clean

banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 18-19, R542: printed pp. 90-91 (pdf 91-92) - the individual area key crosses the volcanic belt: Area 18 the Steam-Heated Caverns (the water-eroded cavern region altered by volcanic upheavals, its sharp fissures tapped into the caves; the meandering river from the Lower Lake reaching a connecting cavern five miles south, the source of a rapid hot stream that joins the river as the riverbed descends; the wide fine-sand shoreline landing for boats; the artificially expanded, straightened chute tunnel racing hot water into the river; the six large caves joined by narrow passages, steamy air, coated rock, boiling-to-cool pools and the slippery mildew; the north tunnel to Area 21 with its once-an-hour superheated blasts, 2% per round cumulative, 4d6 halved on a breath save; the east-tunnel stream inflicting 4d6 per round; the Plane of Fire spillover - efreet, fire elementals, salamanders, fire bats; the hell hounds, rats, green slime, crawlers and megalo centipedes; the fire giants holding sway, their nomadic clan numbering over 50; the half-usual fatigue in the muggy air; and the geysers - a 20% pool susceptibility, 6d6 halved on a save), and Area 19 the Chambers of Fire (the caves baked by the geothermal sources; the swept-clean approach tunnel at 1d6 per turn, dousing to avoid; the roughly circular caverns split by thousands-of-feet floor fissures belching smoke, poison gas, steam and fire once per hour at 25% per type for 1d6 rounds; the dangerous cave heat at 1d6 per round, halved by dousing; the eruption volley - 6d6 per round from steam or fire halved on a breath save, poison gas save-or-die, 1d4 turns of smoke at the page 36 effects; the slender stone arches at 50% over the 3d6-foot fissures; the four mephit forms at 50% after the matching eruption; the common fire bats; the diving magmen; the breathable but smoky air and the mildew; and the remote cavern where the toiling mephits widen the 20-foot fissure with their fireproof pickaxes, 21-40 of them entering per eruption, throwing intruders in as offerings to bring through a monstrously evil creature of the dark lower planes).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~11485-11685) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 206 and 208 = the printed pp. 90-91 windows); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the five-mile junction, the six caves, the 2%-cumulative blast with its 4d6, the 4d6 stream, the 50-giant clan, the 20%/6d6 geysers, the 1d6-per-turn tunnel, the 25% eruption types lasting 1d6 rounds, the 1d6-per-round caves, the 6d6 steam-or-fire, the 1d4-turn smoke, the 50% arches over the 3d6-foot fissures, the four mephit forms at 50%, and the 21-40 (1d20+20) toiling mephits widening the 20-foot fissure; the only garbles settled cross-read (the djvu 296 and 346-foot garbles for the capture 2% and 3d6, the capture ld6/ld4/ld20+20 for the djvu 1d6 and 1d4 and 1d20+20). SEAMS: the R518 water travel (the river junction and the chute), the Monster Manual denizens (the efreet, salamanders, hell hounds, fire giants, mephits, magmen and lava children to come in Area 20), the PHB fire resistance and breath saves, and the page 36 smoke rules. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533-R541 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the junction miles, the cave count, the blast base and step percentages, the dice of the blast, stream and geyser damage, the giant clan size, the fatigue divisor, the geyser pool percentage, the tunnel and cave damage dice, the eruption type percentage and rounds, the eruption damage dice, the smoke turns, the arch percentage, the fissure width dice, the mephit forms and follow percentage, and the toiling-mephit count with its sides and base and the 20-foot fissure width, with the 4d6, 6d6, 1d6, 1d4, 3d6 and 1d20+20 dice pinned as count-sides(-multiplier/base) const pairs or triples. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas. The water-travel/MM/PHB seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnakRiverMeetMiles
consts.comment: the meandering river from the Lower Lake reaches a connecting cavern about five miles south of the main chambers of this area.

consts.name: dnakCaveCount
consts.comment: the main area of caverns contains six large caves.

consts.name: dnakBlastPctBase
consts.comment: the north tunnel to Area 21 is subject to blasts of superheated air about once an hour: a 2% chance per round after a blast (the base chance).

consts.name: dnakBlastPctStep
consts.comment: the superheated-air chance is cumulative - 2% the first round after a blast, 4% the next round, 6% after that, etc. (the step).

consts.name: dnakBlastDmgDice
consts.comment: characters in the north tunnel at the time of a blast sustain 4d6 points of damage (the die count).

consts.name: dnakBlastDmgSides
consts.comment: the superheated-air blast deals 4d6 damage to characters in the tunnel (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakStreamDmgDice
consts.comment: the east-tunnel water inflicts 4d6 points of damage per round (the die count).

consts.name: dnakStreamDmgSides
consts.comment: the east-tunnel water inflicts 4d6 damage per round (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakGiantClanOver
consts.comment: when assembled, the clan of fire giants numbers over 50 individuals.

consts.name: dnakFatigueDiv
consts.comment: the fatigue time divisor: unused characters become fatigued in half the usual time.

consts.name: dnakGeyserPoolPct
consts.comment: a pool of water in this area is 20% likely to be susceptible to geyser activity.

consts.name: dnakGeyserDmgDice
consts.comment: characters caught in the force of one of these geothermal eruptions sustain 6d6 points of damage (the die count).

consts.name: dnakGeyserDmgSides
consts.comment: the geothermal eruption deals 6d6 damage (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakTunnelDmgDice
consts.comment: the approach tunnel is so hot that creatures not resistant to fire sustain 1d6 points of damage per turn (the die count).

consts.name: dnakTunnelDmgSides
consts.comment: the approach tunnel deals 1d6 damage per turn to non-resistant creatures (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakEruptTypePct
consts.comment: an eruption of one of these substances occurs with a 25% chance for any given type.

consts.name: dnakEruptRoundsDice
consts.comment: the eruption lasts for 1d6 rounds (the die count).

consts.name: dnakEruptRoundsSides
consts.comment: the eruption lasts for 1d6 rounds (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakCaveDmgDice
consts.comment: the average temperature in each cave is dangerously hot: creatures not resistant to fire suffer 1d6 points of damage per round (the die count).

consts.name: dnakCaveDmgSides
consts.comment: the cave heat deals 1d6 damage per round to non-resistant creatures (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakEruptDmgDice
consts.comment: the steam or fire eruption deals 6d6 damage per round (the die count).

consts.name: dnakEruptDmgSides
consts.comment: the steam or fire eruption deals 6d6 damage per round (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakSmokeTurnsDice
consts.comment: the smoke eruption fills the cave for 1d4 turns (the die count).

consts.name: dnakSmokeTurnsSides
consts.comment: the smoke eruption fills the cave for 1d4 turns (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakArchPct
consts.comment: there is a 50% chance that a given fissure is bridged in at least one spot by a slender stone arch.

consts.name: dnakFissureWideDice
consts.comment: a given fissure is 3d6 feet wide (the die count).

consts.name: dnakFissureWideSides
consts.comment: a given fissure is 3d6 feet wide (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakMephitForms
consts.comment: mephits, the most common denizens, are represented in all four of their forms: fire, lava, smoke and steam.

consts.name: dnakMephitFollowPct
consts.comment: mephits are 50% likely to be encountered immediately following an eruption of the appropriate type.

consts.name: dnakToilMephitDice
consts.comment: eruptions from the largest fissure bring 21-40 mephits (1d20 + 20) of the appropriate type with the first shock (the die count).

consts.name: dnakToilMephitSides
consts.comment: the toiling mephits number 1d20 + 20 (the die sides).

consts.name: dnakToilMephitBase
consts.comment: the toiling mephits number 1d20 + 20 (the base).

consts.name: dnakFissureWideFt
consts.comment: the mephits aggressively toil to widen the fissure from its current width of 20 feet.

bools.name: dnakVolcanicFissures
bools.comment: the region formed by water erosion has been altered by major subterranean upheavals: fiery volcanic action in nearby sections of Deepearth created sharp fissures throughout the rock, and some of these cracks in the world tapped into the caverns.

bools.name: dnakHotStreamJoin
bools.comment: the connecting cavern is the source of a rapid stream of relatively hot water that joins the river.

bools.name: dnakRiverDescends
bools.comment: the river at this point picks up speed as the riverbed starts to descend more steeply.

bools.name: dnakSandLanding
bools.comment: a wide shoreline coated with a beach of fine sand provides an easy landing for boat traffic.

bools.name: dnakChuteTunnel
bools.comment: the hot-stream tunnel, once a natural cavern, has been artificially expanded to handle an increased flow: its course straightened and its rate of descent increased, so that the hot water races down a veritable chute into the river.

bools.name: dnakNarrowPassages
bools.comment: the six large caves are connected by several narrow passages.

bools.name: dnakSteamyAir
bools.comment: the air is steamy and hot, and water coats all rock surfaces.

bools.name: dnakPoolRange
bools.comment: large pools of water fill the low spots in many of the caverns, their temperatures ranging from boiling hot to relatively cool.

bools.name: dnakMildewSlip
bools.comment: mildew on most of the rock surfaces makes everything extremely slippery.

bools.name: dnakBlastSaveHalf
bools.comment: the blast damage can be saved vs. breath weapon for half, and normal fire resistance benefits might reduce it further.

bools.name: dnakStreamPartial
bools.comment: the east tunnel is the source of the outflowing stream, and the water there inflicts 4d6 points of damage per round with saves as above; characters only partly immersed take the damage reduced accordingly.

bools.name: dnakFireHaven
bools.comment: a favorite haven for creatures who love fire and heat.

bools.name: dnakPlaneSpillover
bools.comment: the Area 21 connection to the Elemental Plane of Fire has enabled creatures from that infernal place to proliferate.

bools.name: dnakPlaneRefugees
bools.comment: efreet, fire elementals, salamanders and fire bats from the Plane of Fire can be encountered here; hostile and aggressive, they are far enough from their escape routes that they will not hesitate to flee an encounter going badly.

bools.name: dnakLesserLairs
bools.comment: hell hounds, giant rats, green slime, carrion crawlers and even megalo centipedes have made these caverns their lairs and fight with normal tenacity.

bools.name: dnakFireGiantSway
bools.comment: the fire giants hold sway over all the other denizens: occasionally accompanied by packs of hell hounds, they restlessly roam bullying the lesser creatures and slaying any who resist; nomadic though they claim the largest cavern as their lair.

bools.name: dnakSteamFatigue
bools.comment: the muggy, oppressive air fatigues characters unused to the environment in half the usual time.

bools.name: dnakNoMinerals
bools.comment: water is plentiful and food in the form of fungi is abundant, but no mineral wealth has been located here.

bools.name: dnakGeysers
bools.comment: several caverns contain geysers capable of spouting scalding water and steam every bit as lethal as a red dragon's breath, and a number of narrow cracks and niches in the rock can issue such deadly blasts.

bools.name: dnakGeyserSaveHalf
bools.comment: a saving throw vs. breath weapon reduces geyser damage to half, and fire resistant benefits can reduce it further.

bools.name: dnakFireBaked
bools.comment: these caves are very close to the fiery geothermal heat sources that constantly bake this portion of Deepearth: formed by water erosion, they now quickly evaporate the small amount of water that flows into them.

bools.name: dnakDryTunnel
bools.comment: the approach tunnel, once a natural cave with a sizable stream, has been swept clean by frequent blasts of tremendous heat and is devoid of cave formations.

bools.name: dnakDouseAvoids
bools.comment: protective measures in the approach tunnel, such as frequently dousing with water, avoid the damage entirely.

bools.name: dnakCircularCaves
bools.comment: the caves formed as a number of large, roughly circular caverns connected by an assortment of artificial and natural tunnels.

bools.name: dnakFloorFissures
bools.comment: each large cave is split by a few long, narrow fissures in the floor, thousands of feet deep.

bools.name: dnakFissureBelch
bools.comment: the fissures often belch out blistering clouds of smoke, poisonous gas, steam and fire, an average of once per hour in each cavern.

bools.name: dnakDouseHalves
bools.comment: protective measures such as water dousing reduce the per-round cave damage to half but do not eliminate it entirely.

bools.name: dnakEruptNoAid
bools.comment: if an eruption occurs while characters are in the cave, mundane protective measures are of no avail.

bools.name: dnakEruptSaveHalf
bools.comment: if steam or fire erupts, characters in the cavern sustain 6d6 points of damage per round, a save vs. breath weapon reducing this to half.

bools.name: dnakPoisonDeath
bools.comment: if poison gas erupts, a saving throw vs. poison is necessary to avoid death.

bools.name: dnakSmokeEffects
bools.comment: smoke eruptions fill the cave for 1d4 turns, with the effects described on page 36 of the DSG.

bools.name: dnakUnearthlyOnly
bools.comment: most earthly creatures are unable to survive the fiery environment; three types of unearthly creatures reside in the area.

bools.name: dnakLavaGasLink
bools.comment: lava mephits are associated with poisonous gas eruptions for this purpose.

bools.name: dnakMephitPurpose
bools.comment: the mephits are generally sent to the Prime Plane to accomplish some fiendish or demonic purpose, but seem to frequent the area simply because they like it; they cheerfully attack earthly creatures, and only in the remote cavern do they pursue a goal.

bools.name: dnakFireBatsCommon
bools.comment: fire bats are also common, flapping about and swooping adroitly into and out of the fissures; they extend their flights into the approaching caverns but do not remain away from their fiery heat sources for long.

bools.name: dnakMagmenDive
bools.comment: groups of magmen climb the sheer walls of the fissures from the furnaces below to joyously leap back down, plummeting thousands of feet into the molten rock; they spend several days per climb, eagerly ignite creatures and objects to gratify their sense of fun, and would enjoy persuading others into the diving game - so far they have found no takers.

bools.name: dnakBadAir
bools.comment: the air is smoky, smells bad and occasionally becomes poisonous, but a series of narrow ceiling fissures vents most of the foul air, so enough fresh air flows in to keep the atmosphere breathable.

bools.name: dnakMildewOnly
bools.comment: mildew has formed in some of the cooler out-of-the-way places - the only form of plant life in the area.

bools.name: dnakMephitOfferings
bools.comment: in the most remote cavern the mephits delight in attacking intruders, dragging them to the largest fissure and throwing them in as offerings; they toil to widen it enough for a monstrously evil creature from one of the dark lower planes, and will continue for many years until they achieve their goal or a major catastrophe seals the fissure.

bools.name: dnakFireproofTools
bools.comment: the mephits chip away with an assortment of superhardened metal tools lying about the cavern - small pickaxes with stone handles and metal picks, completely impervious to fire.
